title: IPO - Maximize Capital
hints: at any moment, the best move is always to take the highest-profit project you can currently afford - but 'currently affordable' changes as your capital grows
sort all projects by their required capital ascending, and keep a pointer that only ever moves forward as your capital increases

maintain a max-heap of profits for every project that has become affordable so far (pointer has passed it); each time your capital grows, advance the pointer to add newly affordable projects to the heap

repeat k times: advance the pointer for any newly affordable projects, pop the max-profit project from the heap and add its profit to your capital. if the heap is ever empty, no more projects can be taken, so stop early
commonMistakes: rescanning all projects for affordability every round instead of using a sorted pointer that only moves forward, which is much slower
forgetting to advance the pointer again after capital grows within the same round before checking the heap
not stopping early when the heap is empty and no more projects are affordable, continuing to loop k times unnecessarily

content.problemStatement:
You're running a company that can take on at most `k` projects before
going public, and you currently have `w` units of capital. You're given
two lists of the same length, `profits` and `capital`, where project i
requires at least `capital[i]` units of capital to start, and once
completed adds `profits[i]` units to your capital permanently.

**Choose which projects to take (up to `k` total, never repeating one)
to maximize your final capital, and return that maximum final
capital.**

You may only work on one project at a time and cannot start a project
you can't currently afford, but once a project is completed its profit
becomes available capital for starting later projects.
notes: starting capital too low to afford any project at all
k = 0, taking no projects, returning the starting capital unchanged
k larger than the number of available projects, so all of them eventually get taken
multiple projects requiring exactly the same capital

sampleTestCases.explanation: start with capital 0, so only project 0 (needs 0) is affordable; completing it gives capital 1; now projects 1 and 2 (each needing 1) are affordable, so take project 2 for the higher profit of 3, ending at capital 1 + 3 = 4
take project 0 (capital 0 -> 1), then project 1 becomes affordable (capital 1 -> 3), then project 2 becomes affordable (capital 3 -> 6); all three projects fit within k = 3
every project requires at least 1 unit of capital to start, but you begin with 0, so no project is ever affordable and your capital stays at 0

optimal.time: O(n log n + k log n)
optimal.pattern: sort projects by required capital, then use a max-heap of profits among currently affordable projects

bruteForce.approach: for each of the k rounds, scan every remaining project to find all currently affordable ones and pick the one with the highest profit, redoing the full scan every round
